newsitem.title: UK: Elvis soap king wins copyright battle in U.K.
newsitem.headline: Elvis soap king wins copyright battle in U.K.

text.p: A British entrepreneur on Tuesday won his legal battle for the right to sell Elvis Presley toiletries in Britain and declared afterwards: "Elvis belongs to the people."
Sid Shaw was jubilant after defeating the mighty Elvis Presley Enterprises of Memphis, Tennesse, which had sought a monopoly on the sale of Elvis souvenirs in Britain.
"We wooped (thrashed) them," said Shaw, an east London entrepreneur who has been selling Elvis memorabilia at his shop 'Elvisly Yours' since 1979.
He was speaking to reporters outside the High Court after Judge Hugh Laddie ruled that he could sell Elvis toiletries under the trademarks Elvis, Elvis Presley, and the Elvis Signature.

But the ruling only applied to the sale of Elvis toiletries and could open the way for the U.S. company to try to prevent Shaw selling other kinds of souvenirs of the pop star, who died of a heart attack in 1977.
Shaw said judge Laddie had been made the honourary president of several Elvis fan clubs in the United States for what he called his part in giving Elvis back to the people.
"You cannot own famous names," said Shaw, who sells Elvis soap, statues and underpants from a range of 2,000 items. "If you could own Elvis you could own Shakespeare."
He was banned from selling his goods in the United States in 1987 but said he always thought he would be allowed to sell them in his native country.
Asked if he thought Elvis was listening in during the court hearing, Shaw said: "He was up there somewhere. 'Kick ass' was what he was probably singing."
